config.classes_note: Two classes, sourced from the field by locus (B1, the card, and B2, the census's saved copy of the same page, hold one text): the inventory as a record of collective bargaining over workplace technology, its unit the union contract provision (title; Overview; sections 2 and 3), which is the census's intersection 'worker-power' and evidence kind 'negotiated provision' as the field states them; and the object those provisions govern, employer use of technology to monitor and manage work (section 4; FAQ on keyword search), which is the census's intersection 'ai-governing-labor' as the field states it. The census's kind, 'searchable inventory', is the field's own phrase ('This searchable inventory') but names no class the archive could apply a category to, and is not run. The archive's instruments of labor direction (Directionality of Semantic Labor, #771; the directionality stack; user labor drag) are the census's lv_intersection, an archive reading, and are not run as classes: no field source places the inventory under them (brief addendum, item 7); where a candidate applies them to a sourced class it is read. The aliases are the entity's short name (the address), its host, its compiler (Lisa Kresge, B1 'researched and developed by Lisa Kresge'), and its operator under both names (UC Berkeley Labor Center; Center for Labor Research and Education, B1 citation). The phrase 'negotiating tech' as salary negotiation is a homonym and not an alias; the alias pattern will meet it, and reading rejects it. Admission by reading (§3.4): a candidate is admitted when its sentence or paragraph makes a claim bearing on the inventory, or applies an archive category to collective bargaining over workplace technology, or to employer governance of work through technology, as a class; a bare mention of collective bargaining or of surveillance in another sense (state, platform or retrieval surveillance; bargaining as a figure) is not a claim on the entity or its classes.
